stem: In the past the number of accidents per month on a certain road was modelled by a random variable with distribution $\text{Po}(0.47)$. After the introduction of speed restrictions, the government wished to test, at the 5% significance level, whether the mean number of accidents had decreased. They noted the number of accidents during the next 12 months. It is assumed that accidents occur randomly and that a Poisson model is still appropriate.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Given that the total number of accidents during the 12 months was 2, carry out the test.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a Type II error in this context.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: It is given that the mean number of accidents per month is now in fact 0.05.
parts.text: Using another random sample of 12 months the same test is carried out again, with the same significance level. Find the probability of a Type II error.
